title: MAPT Sensor Removal and Installation
introduction:
This procedure covers the manifold absolute pressure and temperature (MAPT) sensor on the 3.7L Duratec. The drawing shows the blue sensor on the intake manifold, with its electrical connector and retaining fastener highlighted in magenta.

I think of these as two separate ties to undo: the electrical connection and the mechanical attachment. Disconnect the connector before removing the retainer and sensor; reconnect it after the sensor is secured during refitting. This is a removal and installation guide, with no sensor diagnosis or electrical testing included.

items.name: Confirm engine applicability
items.detail: Use this procedure for the stated engine configuration and identify the sensor against the supplied intake-manifold illustration.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display at Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around the vehicle. Otherwise it could be remotely started at any time, causing personal injury or death. Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from accidentally starting the engine; an accidental start during service may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Protect eyes, ears and hands
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged components. Failure to use the required protection may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Inspect cooling fans before underhood work
items.detail: With the ignition OFF, inspect all cooling fans for damage, cracks or separation. Do not work under the hood with a damaged fan; replace it with a new one before proceeding. A damaged fan can separate during operation and cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Disable fans before working nearby
items.detail: Fans may run with the ignition off. If access brings you near a cooling fan, disable the fans before working there; unexpected operation may cause personal injury. Have the applicable disabling instructions available if this precaution is needed.

items.name: Use a suitable torque wrench
items.detail: Have a torque wrench capable of applying the sensor-retainer installation specification given in the removal step.

edits.text: NOTE: Read the removal steps before starting; they may also contain details needed for installation.
edits.why: The retainer's installation torque is given beside its removal instruction.

edits.text: Disconnect the MAPT sensor electrical connector identified in the illustration before releasing the sensor's mechanical attachment.
edits.why: The magenta connector identifies the electrical connection, while the separate highlighted fastener secures the sensor. Disconnecting first frees the sensor from the wiring connection before removal.

edits.text: Remove the retainer, then remove the MAPT sensor from the intake manifold. During installation, tighten the retainer to 35 lb.in (4 Nm).
edits.why: The blue component is the sensor, and the magenta fastener marks its retaining attachment. The torque applies to refitting the retainer, not to loosening it.

edits.text: NOTE: A second fastener hole is available for use during reinstallation if needed.
edits.why: This preserves the optional fastening location for refitting. No additional criterion for choosing that hole is specified.

edits.text: Install by reversing removal: refit the MAPT sensor, install and tighten the retainer to the specification given above, then reconnect the electrical connector. Use the alternate fastener hole if needed, as noted above.
edits.why: I finish by accounting for both connections shown in the drawing: the sensor must be mechanically secured and its electrical connector reconnected. These completion checks confirm reassembly; they do not establish whether the sensor was faulty.
